title: Palm Sugar Lime Shrimp Skewers
seoTitle: Palm Sugar Lime Shrimp Skewers | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Shrimp skewer night—palm sugar lime lacquer, fast char, no generic kabob repeat
subtitle: Palm sugar–lime glazed jumbo shrimp with Thai basil, fried shallots, and char for ten
description: Colossal shrimp take a 30-minute lime-shallot marinade, hit a 450°F grate for two minutes a side, and get lacquered with a palm sugar–nam pla–tamarind glaze in the final minute — finished with Thai basil and fried shallots.

steps.title: Simmer the palm sugar glaze
steps.instruction: Melt the palm sugar with 2 tablespoons of water in a small saucepan over medium-low, then stir in the nam pla, tamarind concentrate, minced Thai bird chilies, and shredded kaffir lime leaves. Simmer 3–4 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon, then pull it — it thickens more as it cools, and a glaze that sets hard drags off the brush. You want sweet, salty, sour, and hot fighting each other in one spoonful.

steps.title: Marinate the shrimp — 30 minutes, no longer
steps.instruction: Toss the shrimp with the minced shallots, the juice of two limes, a tablespoon of the glaze, and a pinch of salt, then refrigerate 20–30 minutes. Set a timer: lime acid starts cooking the outside like ceviche past the half hour, and over-marinated shrimp turn mushy over the fire instead of snapping.

steps.title: Thread them flat
steps.instruction: Thread 4–5 shrimp per skewer, running the point through both the thick head end and the tail of each one so they lie flat — flat shrimp make full contact and char, while curled shrimp bridge the grate and steam in their own gaps. Pat the loaded skewers dry with paper towel; surface water is the enemy of char on a two-minute cook.

steps.title: Get the grate screaming and slicked
steps.instruction: Preheat the grill to high, 450–500°F at the grate, lid down for 8 minutes. Scrub the grates clean, then wipe them with grapeseed oil on a folded paper towel held in tongs — grapeseed's high smoke point survives where olive oil burns to varnish. At this heat, anything that sticks tears.

steps.title: Grill the shrimp two minutes a side
steps.instruction: Lay the skewers over direct heat and grill 2 minutes per side. Done is pink with charred edges, opaque all the way through, and 145°F on an instant-read thermometer in the thickest shrimp — colossal shrimp can hide a translucent center behind a charred shell, so always check the fattest one. Thirty seconds past that and they start turning to erasers.

steps.title: Lacquer with glaze over the flame
steps.instruction: Brush the glaze on both sides of the skewers and give them 30 seconds per side more, until sticky and glossy with a few caramelized spots. Palm sugar scorches fast — if flames chase the drips, slide the skewers to the cooler edge and finish there. Glazing at the end keeps the char clean and the lacquer bright.

steps.title: Shower with basil and fried shallots
steps.instruction: Pile the skewers on platters and scatter the torn Thai basil and fried shallots over while the shrimp are hot — the heat blooms the basil into fragrance, and the shallots only stay crunchy if they land at service. Lime wedges on the side; about 8 oz of shrimp per firefighter.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover the shrimp skewers — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool the shrimp skewers and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Set a timer on the marinade — lime acid ceviches the surface past 30 minutes and the texture never recovers.
Palm sugar glaze sets hard as it cools; 20 seconds back over low flame loosens it before brushing.
No kaffir lime leaves? Double the lime zest into the glaze — different perfume, same lift.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.
tonightSpread: Main: palm sugar lime shrimp skewers with Thai basil and fried shallots
Sides: coconut rice, quick cucumber salad
Condiments: lime wedges, reserved glaze as a dip
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool the shrimp skewers in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Leftover shrimp eat better cold than reheated — pull them for lettuce wraps or toss into fried rice off the heat at the end.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Ten minutes of fire from grate to platter, and the sweet-hot lacquer with crunchy fried shallots makes these vanish faster than any kebab night — the kind of cook you can still start when a tone feels likely.
substitutions: Honey swaps 1:1 for palm sugar with a squeeze of sriracha for heat — that's the classic honey-sriracha version of this same skewer.
Any fish sauce is nam pla — use whatever bottle the pantry has.
Jumbo (21/25) shrimp work fine; drop to 90 seconds per side and watch the 145°F mark.
One serrano stands in for two bird chilies at about half the heat.
mealPrepNotes: The glaze holds a week refrigerated — make it ahead and reserve some clean for dipping. Marinate 20–30 minutes max, thread flat, grill 2 minutes a side at 450°F+, glaze in the final minute. Hold covered no more than 12 minutes or the shrimp tighten.
